sections.skill: Choose and use payment methods safely: checks, electronic transfers, and payment apps

questions.prompt: Nora writes a check for $1,254.07. How should she write the amount in words on the check?

choices.text: One thousand two hundred fifty-four and 07/100 dollars
One thousand two hundred fifty-four and 7/10 dollars
Twelve hundred fifty-four point zero seven
One thousand two hundred forty-five and 07/100 dollars

questions.correct_answer: One thousand two hundred fifty-four and 07/100 dollars
questions.intro: A check is a written order telling your bank to pay someone from your account. You write the date, the payee (who gets paid), the amount in numbers, the amount in words with cents as a fraction of 100, and your signature. The words are the legal amount if the two differ.
questions.feedback: $1,254.07 is written "One thousand two hundred fifty-four and 07/100 dollars."

misconceptions.C: Uses "point" instead of the cents fraction

sources: CFPB (Regulation E): Report unauthorized electronic transfers that appear on a statement within 60 days of the statement date to keep liability limits. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

questions.prompt: Ben receives a paycheck made out to him and wants to deposit it at an ATM. What should he write on the back?

choices.text: Nothing; endorsing a check is optional
His PIN, so the ATM can verify him
His account balance, so the bank can update it
His signature and "For deposit only"

questions.intro: To deposit or cash a check made out to you, you "endorse" it by signing the back. Adding "For deposit only" (a restrictive endorsement) means the check can only be deposited, which protects it if it is lost. For mobile deposit, banks often require "For mobile deposit only" too.
questions.feedback: Signing with "For deposit only" endorses the check and limits it to being deposited.

misconceptions.B: Writes sensitive data on a check
misconceptions.C: Thinks the balance goes on the check

questions.prompt: Mia sends $60 through a payment app to someone selling concert tickets online. The tickets never arrive. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The app must refund every payment that goes wrong
Her bank will reverse the payment automatically within one business day
The seller must legally deliver the tickets
Payments she authorized are often hard or impossible to reverse

questions.correct_answer: Payments she authorized are often hard or impossible to reverse
questions.intro: Peer-to-peer (P2P) payment apps move money quickly between people. Money you send yourself, even to a scammer, is usually treated as authorized and is often hard to get back. Federal error protections focus on transfers you did not authorize. Use P2P apps mainly with people you know and trust.
questions.feedback: Because Mia authorized the payment, getting it back depends on the app's or bank's voluntary policies. Protections are stronger for unauthorized transfers.

misconceptions.C: Thinks the law forces a scammer to deliver

sources: CFPB (Regulation E): Report unauthorized electronic transfers that appear on a statement within 60 days of the statement date to keep liability limits. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

questions.prompt: After depositing a check with his phone, what should Kai do with the paper check?

choices.text: Keep it until the deposit is final, then destroy it
Deposit the same check again at the bank to be safe
Throw it in the trash right after taking the photo
Give it back to the person who wrote it

questions.correct_answer: Keep it until the deposit is final, then destroy it
questions.intro: Mobile check deposit lets you photograph a signed check in your bank's app. The bank may hold part of the money for a few days. Keep the paper check until the deposit is final, then destroy it securely so it cannot be deposited twice or misused.
questions.feedback: Keep it until the funds are final in case the bank needs it, then shred it.

misconceptions.C: Discards it before the deposit is confirmed

questions.prompt: Zara's landlord asks for rent in a way that leaves a record of payment. Which method fits BEST?

choices.text: A check or an electronic transfer from her bank account
Cash handed over without a receipt
A gift card code sent by text
A wire transfer to an account number she has never verified

questions.correct_answer: A check or an electronic transfer from her bank account
questions.feedback: Checks and bank transfers leave records Zara can use as proof of payment.

sections.relationship: Choosing a payment method safely requires knowing what each method is and where the money comes from.

questions.prompt: Which payment method moves money directly from your bank account electronically on a date you set?

choices.text: A paper check that the store mails to you each month
A credit card
A store gift card
An online bill payment or automatic transfer

questions.correct_answer: An online bill payment or automatic transfer
questions.intro: Common ways to pay: cash; debit cards and checks (from your account); electronic transfers such as online bill pay and automatic payments (from your account, electronically); credit cards (borrowed money); and prepaid or gift cards (money loaded in advance).
questions.feedback: Online bill pay and automatic payments take money from your account electronically.

misconceptions.B: Confuses borrowing with paying from your account
misconceptions.C: Confuses prepaid value with an account payment

sources: CFPB (Regulation E): Report unauthorized electronic transfers that appear on a statement within 60 days of the statement date to keep liability limits. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

questions.prompt: Which method gives the LEAST proof that you paid?

choices.text: A check that the bank later shows as cleared
A debit card purchase listed on the statement
An online bill payment with a confirmation number
Cash with no receipt

questions.intro: A payment record proves you paid. Bank statements, cleared checks, and confirmation numbers are records. Cash leaves no record unless you get a receipt.
questions.feedback: Cash without a receipt leaves no proof of payment.

misconceptions.A: A cleared check is a record

questions.prompt: A gift card loaded with $50 is used to buy a $12 item. What is left on the card?
questions.intro: A prepaid or gift card holds a set amount of money. Each purchase is subtracted until the card reaches $0.

misconceptions.C: Thinks the card balance does not change
misconceptions.A: Confuses the price with what is left

questions.prompt: Who is the "payee" on a check?

choices.text: The person or business that receives the money
The account holder who signs and writes the check
The bank that prints the check
The cashier who accepts the check

questions.correct_answer: The person or business that receives the money
questions.feedback: The payee is named on the "Pay to the order of" line.

misconceptions.B: Confuses payee with the account holder

questions.prompt: Which situation makes a payment app MOST risky to use?

choices.text: Paying a stranger online before receiving the item
Splitting a dinner bill with a close friend
Paying a family member back for groceries
Sending rent money to a roommate you have lived with for a year

questions.correct_answer: Paying a stranger online before receiving the item
questions.feedback: Paying strangers in advance is how many P2P scams work, because payments are hard to reverse.

sections.skill: Wires, ACH transfers, and official checks

questions.prompt: Which payment is generally the hardest to reverse once sent?

choices.text: A credit card purchase
A check that has not been cashed yet
A debit card purchase you did not authorize
A wire transfer

questions.intro: A wire transfer moves money between banks quickly, often the same day, and is generally final once sent. ACH transfers (used for direct deposit and online bill pay) move money between bank accounts more slowly and have some ways to return errors. Scammers often ask for wires because they are fast and hard to reverse.
questions.feedback: Wires are fast and generally final, which is why scammers prefer them.

misconceptions.B: A stop payment may be possible

sources: CFPB (Regulation E): Report unauthorized electronic transfers that appear on a statement within 60 days of the statement date to keep liability limits. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

questions.prompt: A buyer sends Liam a cashier's check for $1,500 for a $500 phone and asks him to wire back the extra $1,000. What is most likely happening?

choices.text: A fake-check scam
A generous buyer making an honest mistake
A normal practice for cashier's checks
A bank error that the bank will cover

questions.intro: A cashier's check is drawn on the bank's own funds, so a real one is very reliable. But fake cashier's checks are common. The bank may make the money available before discovering the check is fake; when it bounces, you owe the bank the full amount.
questions.feedback: Overpayment with a request to send money back is a classic fake-check scam. Liam would owe the bank when the check bounces.

misconceptions.B: Ignores the classic overpayment scam pattern
misconceptions.D: Thinks the bank absorbs fraud losses

questions.prompt: Which is a typical use of an ACH transfer?

choices.text: Buying groceries with cash
Paying a bill with a paper money order bought at a store
Swiping a credit card at a store
An employer's direct deposit of paychecks

questions.correct_answer: An employer's direct deposit of paychecks
questions.intro: The ACH (Automated Clearing House) network moves money electronically between bank accounts in batches. It is cheaper and slower than a wire transfer.
questions.feedback: Direct deposit and many automatic bill payments use the ACH network.
sources: CFPB (Regulation E): Report unauthorized electronic transfers that appear on a statement within 60 days of the statement date to keep liability limits. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

questions.prompt: Before wiring money for a home or apartment deposit, what is the safest step?

choices.text: Use the instructions in the most recent email, even if they changed
Wire the money quickly so you do not lose the apartment
Ask the sender to text you the account number again
Call a phone number you already know is real to confirm the instructions

questions.correct_answer: Call a phone number you already know is real to confirm the instructions
questions.intro: Criminals hack or fake emails and send new "updated" wire instructions so money goes to their account. Because wires are hard to reverse, verify instructions through a trusted phone number, not one in the suspicious email.

misconceptions.C: Uses the same possibly hacked channel

questions.prompt: Ruth wrote a check and then learned it was lost in the mail before it was cashed. What service could stop it?

choices.text: A stop payment order through her bank
A wire recall, which works on all checks
Reporting the check to the IRS
Writing a second check for the same amount

questions.correct_answer: A stop payment order through her bank
questions.intro: Until a check is paid by your bank, you can ask the bank not to pay it. Banks usually charge a fee for this service, and it does not work on a check that has already cleared.
questions.feedback: A stop payment order tells the bank not to pay that check, if it has not already cleared.
sources: CFPB (Regulation E): Report unauthorized electronic transfers that appear on a statement within 60 days of the statement date to keep liability limits. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

questions.prompt: Someone texts Ava: "I sent you $200 by mistake — please send it back!" Her app shows no new money in her account. What should she do?

choices.text: Check her own account directly and send nothing
Send $200 back right away to be polite
Reply with her bank login so they can fix it
Send $100 as a compromise

questions.correct_answer: Check her own account directly and send nothing
questions.intro: A common scam claims you received money "by mistake" and asks you to send it back. Sometimes the original payment was made with stolen information and is later reversed, leaving you with the loss. Verify inside your own app or bank, never through a link or message.
questions.feedback: Without verified money in her own account, there is nothing to return. Even if money did arrive, contact the app's support rather than sending money.

misconceptions.D: Still sends money to a scammer

questions.prompt: Which setting adds the most protection to a payment app?

choices.text: Sharing your login with a parent and a friend so they can watch for fraud
Using the same password as your email
Turning off notifications
Multi-factor authentication and a passcode on the app

questions.correct_answer: Multi-factor authentication and a passcode on the app
questions.feedback: Multi-factor authentication and an app passcode make unauthorized access much harder.

questions.prompt: A "customer support" caller says your payment app is hacked and asks you to send your balance to a "safe account." What is this?

choices.text: A standard security procedure
A government requirement
A normal account-security check
An imposter scam

questions.intro: Real banks and payment apps do not ask you to move money to a "safe account" to protect it. Imposters pretend to be bank staff, tech support, or government officials and create urgency.
questions.feedback: Any request to move money to protect it is a red flag for an imposter scam. Hang up and call the official number.

misconceptions.A: Real companies do not ask this
misconceptions.C: Believes real support asks for codes

questions.prompt: Which payment is generally protected under federal error rules (Regulation E)?

choices.text: A transfer someone else made from your account without permission
A payment you chose to send to an online seller who never shipped
A payment you sent to the wrong person after typing their name
Money you lost gambling with an app

questions.correct_answer: A transfer someone else made from your account without permission
questions.feedback: Regulation E protections focus on unauthorized transfers and certain errors; payments you authorize, even to scammers, are often not covered.

questions.prompt: Before sending money with a payment app to someone new, which step lowers the risk the MOST?

choices.text: Sending a small test payment to a stranger
Checking that the stranger's profile has a photo and many friends
Asking the stranger to promise to deliver
Confirming who the recipient is through a source you trust

questions.correct_answer: Confirming who the recipient is through a source you trust
questions.feedback: Verifying who you are paying, through a channel you trust, prevents most P2P losses.
